s1.syndrome_frame: febrile neutropenic patient with cutaneous lesions and evidence of disseminated infection
salient_findings: vesicles with erythematous base on the lower back and left thigh
evidence of filamentous bacilli on histopathology
key_facts: female infant with history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia
admitted for reinduction chemotherapy
became febrile 17 days after last day of chemotherapy
neutropenic at the time of fever
had an indwelling catheter
vesicles with erythematous base observed on the lower back and left thigh
tissue and blood cultures were obtained
punch biopsy of vesicle on lower back was performed
microscopic examination showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis
numerous filamentous bacilli with septa seen on hematoxylin-eosin stain
gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis
periodic acid-Schiff staining was negative for fungal elements
PCR testing for HSV and VZV were negative
CT scan with contrast showed lesions in the liver and brain

shortlist.label: Bacillus cereus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Gram stain revealed gram-variable rods and presence of filamentous bacilli with septa, consistent with Bacillus cereus

shortlist.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection
shortlist.why_kept: Febrile neutropenic patient with cutaneous lesions, a common presentation for Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection

shortlist.label: Nocardia infection
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of filamentous bacilli with septa on histopathology, a characteristic feature of Nocardia infection

shortlist.label: Clostridium septicum infection
shortlist.why_kept: Neutropenic patient with evidence of disseminated infection and cutaneous lesions, a possible presentation for Clostridium septicum infection

shortlist.label: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia infection
shortlist.why_kept: Opportunistic infection in immunocompromised patients, particularly those with indwelling catheters, which is consistent with the patient's history

raw.rationale: Numerous filamentous bacilli with septa seen on hematoxylin-eosin stain and gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis are characteristic of Nocardia infection

rejected.label: Bacillus cereus infection
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic features of Bacillus cereus infection in the provided histopathology

rejected.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection
rejected.why: Gram stain typically shows gram-negative rods, not gram-variable rods

rejected.label: Clostridium septicum infection
rejected.why: Typically associated with gas gangrene and not characterized by filamentous bacilli with septa

rejected.label: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia infection
rejected.why: Not typically associated with skin lesions and filamentous bacilli with septa
